### Observed differences

- In the later window, five activities that were absent or nearly absent earlier — A19, A20, A25, A26, A27, each seen in 0–2 of 200 earlier traces — each run in about 18–23 of 100 traces. Their shares add up to essentially every later trace, and pairs of them almost never share a trace (co-occurrence at most about 0.5 in 100), so a later trace contains essentially exactly one of the five, at around 0.4 of the trace's event positions. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL009, REL017, REL024, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

- This stage sits between A43 and A28. Earlier, A43 led directly to A28 in about 95 of 100 of its outgoing transitions, one event apart; in the later window, A43 leads to one of the five in about 97 of 100 (about 18–22 each), each of the five leads on to A28 in about 95–100 of 100, the direct A43→A28 share falls to about 1 in 100, and the A43→A28 distance becomes two events in about 97 of 100 cases. The five run after A43 and before A28 in about 22 of 100 traces each. [DIR007, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG002, REL013, REL014, REL020, REL021]

- A06 also changed: it appears in about 27 of 100 later traces versus about 9 earlier; its position moved from mid-trace (mean about 0.54) to the end (median about 0.97); A48 now routes to A06 in about 24 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 2–3 earlier) and A06 routes to A49 in about 89 of 100 (about 26 earlier, previously spread over many successors), sitting one event before A49 in about 95 of 100 later cases (based on only 6 earlier cases). A48, A28 and A43 each precede A06 in about 24 of 100 later traces, versus about 2–5 earlier. [OCC001, POS001, DIR008, DIR001, LAG001, LAG003, REL006, REL007, REL008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the process runs a stage of five mutually exclusive activities — A19, A20, A25, A26, A27 — between A43 and A28, where A43 previously led directly to A28: A43 now routes to one of the five (together about 97 of 100 of its outgoing transitions), that activity then leads to A28, and the A43→A28 distance moves from one event to two, with each alternative taken in roughly 18–23 of 100 traces and exactly one of the five in essentially every later trace. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, LAG002, REL009, REL013, REL014, REL020, REL021, REL024]

The reading is direct and consistent: relational items place A43 before the alternative and the alternative before A28, the distance item shows the one-to-two step shift on the A43→A28 pair, and direction items show A43 rerouting to the five and the five converging on A28; with 50 qualifying control-flow items against fewer than one expected without change, the evidence set as a whole is far beyond what a stable process typically produces. [LAG002, REL013, REL014, REL020, REL021, DIR007, DIR002]

Limitations: positions are event ranks, not clock times, so no timing claim is made; and the evidence cannot fully exclude that the five activities existed earlier as an extremely rare path (A27 appeared in 2 of 200 earlier traces) that later became the only route through this segment — the near-collapse of the direct A43→A28 edge (about 95 to about 1 in 100) shows the routing through it changed regardless. [OCC006, DIR007, LAG002]

Other differences: A06 now runs between A48 and A49 in about a quarter of later traces — A48 routes to A06 in about 24 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 2–3 earlier), A06 then leads to A49 in about 89 of 100, A06's participation rose from about 9 to about 27 of 100 traces with its position moving from mid-trace to the end, and A48 precedes A06 in about 24 of 100 traces (about 2 earlier). This concerns a different part of the process than the A43–A28 change, and A06 shares a trace with each of the five alternatives in only about 4–6 of 100 cases. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR008, LAG001, LAG003, REL008, REL001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 137 units tested, 50 items qualified, 0.68 expected by chance. That's a huge excess — 50 items vs fewer than 1 expected. So the count is many times larger than chance expectation. This means the evidence as a whole cannot be explained by chance. So we move beyond "insufficient evidence" based on the screening comparison.

Now, what do the items show?

OCC items (occurrence):
- OCC001: A06 participation rose from 0.09 (about 9 in 100 traces) to 0.265 (about 27 in 100). Mean occurrences per trace 0.095 → 0.27. Support 18 before, 53 after.
- OCC002: A19 from 0 to 0.22 (44 traces after, 0 before).
- OCC003: A20 from 0 to 0.225 (45 after).
- OCC004: A25 from 0 to 0.19 (37 after).
- OCC005: A26 from 0 to 0.195 (39 after).
- OCC006: A27 from 0.01 to 0.175 (2 before, 35 after).

So five activities (A19, A20, A25, A26, A27) were essentially absent before (0–2 traces out of 200) and now appear in roughly 18–23% of traces. A06 rose from ~9% to ~27%.

DIR items:
- DIR001: A06's outgoing transitions: before spread across many successors (A49 26%, A15 16%, A16 11%, others ~5%); after, A49 dominates at ~89%. So A06 now almost always leads to A49.
- DIR002: A19's outgoing: after, ~98% to A28. Before empty (A19 not observed).
- DIR003: A20 → A28 ~98% after.
- DIR004: A25 → A28 ~95% after.
- DIR005: A26 → A28 ~97% after.
- DIR006: A27: before went to A44/A33 (50/50, only 2 observations), after 100% to A28.
- DIR007: A43's outgoing: before ~95% to A28; after redistributed: A20 22%, A19 20%, A26 19.5%, A25 18%, A27 17.5%, A28 only 1%. So A43 now leads to the new activities instead of directly to A28.
- DIR008: A48's outgoing: A49 95% → 76%, A06 2.5% → 24%. So A48 now sometimes leads to A06.

POS items:
- POS001: A06 position: before mean ~0.54 (mid-process), after mean ~0.91 (near end). Median 0.44 → 0.97. So A06 moved later in the trace (position-wise).
- POS002–POS005: A19, A20, A25, A26 appear at mean position ~0.38–0.41 after (not observed before).
- POS006: A27 position mean 0.74 → 0.39 (moved earlier), support 2 → 35.
- POS007: A48 position essentially unchanged (mean ~0.96), support 1.0 both windows.

REL items:
- REL001–REL005: A06 with A19/A20/A25/A26/A27: before, co-occurrence 0 (A06 alone in ~9% of traces, neither ~91%); after, co-occurrence ~4.5–6%, B_only ~12–18%, A_only ~21–22%. So they now sometimes occur together, mostly not.
- REL006: A06 & A28: before co-occurrence 9%, B_only 91%; after co-occurrence 26.5%, B_only 73.5%. B_before_A rose from 4% to 24.5%. So A28 before A06 became more common.
- REL007: A06 & A43: similar — co-occurrence 9% → 26.5%, B_before_A 4.5% → 24.5%.
- REL008: A06 & A48: co-occurrence 9% → 26.5%, B_before_A 2% → 23.5%.
- REL009–REL012, REL017–REL019, REL024–REL026: pairs among {A19, A20, A25, A26, A27}: before neither 99–100%; after, A_only ~18–23%, B_only ~17–23%, co-occurrence ~0–0.5%. So these new activities are alternatives — they rarely occur in the same trace.
- REL013: A19 & A28: before B_only 100% (A28 always present, A19 never); after co-occurrence 22%, A_before_B 21.5%. So A19 now occurs before A28 in ~22% of traces.
- REL014: A19 & A43: after co-occurrence 22%, B_before_A 22% (A43 before A19).
- REL015: A19 & A48: co-occurrence 22%, A_before_B 21.5% (A19 before A48).
- REL016: A19 & A49: co-occurrence 22%, A_before_B 22%.
- REL020: A20 & A28: co-occurrence 22.5%, A_before_B 22.5%.
- REL021: A20 & A43: co-occurrence 22.5%, B_before_A 22.5% (A43 before A20).
- REL022: A20 & A48: co-occurrence 22.5%, A_before_B 22.5%.
- REL023: A20 & A49: co-occurrence 22.5%, A_before_B 22.5%.
- LAG001: A06→A49 lag: before lag 1 in 83%, lag 3 in 17%; after lag 1 in 95%. Support 6 before, 49 after.
- LAG002: A43→A28 lag: before lag 1 in 95%; after lag 2 in 96.5%. So A43 to A28 now has one more step in between — consistent with the new activities being inserted between A43 and A28.
- LAG003: A48→A49: lag 1 95% → 76%, lag 2 5% → 24%. Consistent with A06 (and its block) being inserted between A48 and A49 sometimes.

Let me reconstruct the story:

Before: A43 → A28 (directly, 95% of the time, lag 1). A48 → A49 (lag 1, 95%). A06 appears in ~9% of traces, mid-process (mean position 0.54), leading to various successors including A49 (26%).

After: A43 now leads to one of {A19, A20, A25, A26, A27} (~20% each, total ~97%), and each of these leads to A28 (~95–98%). So a new block of alternative activities was inserted between A43 and A28. LAG002 confirms: A43→A28 distance shifted from 1 step to 2 steps.

Also, A06's participation rose from 9% to 26.5%, and its position moved from mid (0.54) to near-end (0.91, median 0.97). A06 now leads to A49 ~89% of the time. A48→A49 sometimes now goes through A06 (A48→A06 rose from 2.5% to 24%), and LAG003 shows A48→A49 distance increased. REL008: A06 & A48 co-occurrence rose from 9% to 26.5%, with A48 before A06 rising from 2% to 23.5%. So A06 is now inserted between A48 and A49 in about a quarter of traces.

Wait — but A06's participation is 26.5% after, and A48→A06 is 24% of A48's outgoing transitions. A48 is in ~100% of traces (POS007 support 1.0). So A48→A06 in ~24% of traces matches A06 participation 26.5%. And A06→A49 89% of A06's outgoing. So the path A48 → A06 → A49 appears in ~22-24% of traces. REL015/REL016: A19 & A48 co-occurrence 22% with A19 before A48... wait, A19 before A48? Hmm.

Wait, REL015: A19 & A48: A_before_B = 0.215, i.e., A19 before A48 in 21.5% of traces. And REL016: A19 & A49: A_before_B 0.22. Hmm, so A19 occurs before A48 and before A49. But A19's position mean is 0.40, A48's is ~0.96. So A19 (position 0.40) before A48 (position 0.96) makes sense.

But DIR007 says A43 → A19 etc. And A43's position? A43 is in ~100% of traces (DIR007 support 201/200). A19 at position 0.40. A28 at... A28 is B_only 78% with A19, co-occurrence 22% with A19 before A28. So the chain: A43 → A19 → A28. And A19 before A48 (A48 near end at 0.96). Hmm, but A48 → A06 → A49 with A06 at position 0.91-0.97.

Wait, let me reconsider. A06's position after: mean 0.91, median 0.97. A48's position: mean 0.957. A49? Not directly given, but A48→A49 lag 1 mostly.

Hmm, so what's the order? Let me think: A43 (somewhere) → A19/A20/A25/A26/A27 (position ~0.4) → A28. And separately A48 (position 0.96) → A06 (position 0.91 median 0.97?) hmm, A06 median 0.97, A48 median 0.967. These are close. REL008: A48 before A06 in 23.5% — B_before_A where B=A48. So A48 before A06. And A06 → A49 89%.

Actually wait, POS001: A06 after mean 0.91, q25 0.966, median 0.969, q75 0.971. So most A06 occurrences are at ~0.97 of the trace. A48 at 0.957 mean. So A48 slightly before A06 typically. A48→A06 24% of outgoing. Then A06→A49.

So the after picture: main flow ... A43 → {A19|A20|A25|A26|A27} → A28 ... A48 → (A06 in ~24%) → A49.

Before picture: A43 → A28 directly (95%, lag 1). A48 → A49 directly (95%, lag 1). A06 rare (9%), mid-process, scattered successors.

So two insertions:
1. A block of five alternative activities (A19, A20, A25, A26, A27) inserted between A43 and A28, each taken in ~18-23% of traces, mutually exclusive (co-occurrence among them ~0). Before, A43 led directly to A28.
2. A06 inserted between A48 and A49 in about a quarter of traces (A48→A06 rose from ~2.5% to ~24%; A06→A49 now ~89%; A48→A49 lag shifted from 1 to mostly 1 but 24% at 2). Before, A06 was a rare mid-process activity with scattered outputs.

Hmm wait, but is A06's increase part of the same hypothesis or a separate one? A06 participation rose from 9% to 26.5%. A48→A06 rose from 2.5% to 24%. Before, A06's incoming was presumably from various places (we don't have incoming direction data — DIR is outgoing only). Before, A06 led to A49 26% of the time (of 19 outgoing transitions observed... support before 19). Actually DIR001 before: A49 0.263, A15 0.158, others ~0.05 each, over 19 outgoing transitions in 18 traces. After: A49 0.889 over 54 outgoing transitions in 53 traces.

So the A06 story: A06 became much more frequent (9% → 26.5% of traces), now sits near the end (position ~0.97), and almost always leads to A49; it typically follows A48. This looks like A06 was inserted into the A48→A49 path.

Are these two separate changes or one? They involve disjoint activity sets mostly: {A19, A20, A25, A26, A27} between A43 and A28; A06 between A48 and A49. A43 and A48 are different activities. A28 and A49 different. So two distinct structural changes.

Actually, wait — could it be one change? Let me check: is there a relation between the new activities and A06? REL001-005 show A06 with each of the new activities: co-occurrence ~4.5-6%, mostly A_only or B_only. So they're largely independent — A06 and the new block occur in different traces mostly. A06 in 26.5%, new block in ~22% each, total new-block participation... A19 22%, A20 22.5%, A25 18.5%, A26 19.5%, A27 17.5% — sum ~100%. So essentially every trace has exactly one of the new activities? Let's check: neither for A19&A20 is 0.555, A_only 0.22, B_only 0.225 — so 44.5% of traces have exactly one of A19/A20. Summing across the five: if each trace has exactly one, pairwise neither would be 1 - (p_i + p_j). For A19 (0.22) and A20 (0.225): neither = 0.555 = 1 - 0.445. Yes! Exactly. So every trace in the after window contains exactly one of the five new activities. And co-occurrence between any pair is ~0.

And before, none of them appeared (neither = 1.0 for pairs). So the new block is now mandatory — every trace passes through exactly one of {A19, A20, A25, A26, A27}, between A43 and A28.

Hmm, but wait — is it between A43 and A28 in every trace? DIR007: A43's outgoing after: A19 20%, A20 22%, A25 18%, A26 19.5%, A27 17.5%, plus small bits (A02, A04, A31, A10 ~0.5% each), A28 1%. Sum of five: 97%. And each new activity leads to A28 at 95-98%. REL013: A19 & A28 co-occurrence 22%, A19 before A28 21.5%. REL020: A20 & A28 co-occurrence 22.5%, A20 before A28 22.5%. So yes, the new activity precedes A28.

And A43 before the new activity: REL014: A19 & A43 co-occurrence 22%, B_before_A 22% (A43 = B, before A19). REL021: A20 & A43: B_before_A 22.5%. So A43 → new activity → A28.

LAG002: A43→A28 lag: before 95% at lag 1; after 96.5% at lag 2. Confirms one activity inserted between A43 and A28.

So hypothesis 1 (strongly supported): a new stage of five alternative activities (A19, A20, A25, A26, A27) was inserted between A43 and A28; before, A43 led directly to A28 (95% at distance 1); after, A43 leads to one of the five (~97% combined), which then leads to A28 (95-98%), at distance 2 (96.5%). The five are mutually exclusive alternatives (pairwise co-occurrence ≤0.5%, exactly one per trace).

Hypothesis 2: A06 became a frequent step between A48 and A49: A48→A06 rose from ~2.5% to ~24% of A48's outgoing transitions; A06 now leads to A49 in ~89% of its outgoing transitions (before ~26%); A06's participation rose from ~9% to ~26.5% of traces and its position moved from mid-trace (mean ~0.54) to near the end (median ~0.97); A48→A49 distance shifted from lag 1 (95%) to lag 1 (76%) / lag 2 (24%). REL008: A48 before A06 in 23.5% of traces (was 2%).

Hmm, but is A06 before A49 in the after window? REL doesn't have A06-A49 pair directly... Actually LAG001 is A06→A49: after, lag 1 in 95% (support 49). Before, lag 1 in 83%, lag 3 in 17% (support 6). So A06 → A49 directly in the after window.

So both changes are insertions of activity/blocks into existing direct edges: A43→A28 got the five-way alternative block; A48→A49 got A06 (in ~24% of cases).

Now, how to frame the main hypothesis? The instructions say: state one main hypothesis first, name the activities and how their behaviour changed. Other differences go under "Other differences:".

The dominant change (by item count) is the insertion of the five alternatives between A43 and A28. That's supported by OCC002-006, DIR002-007, POS002-006, REL009-026, LAG002. The A06 change is supported by OCC001, DIR001, DIR008, POS001, POS007 (weak), REL001-008, LAG001, LAG003.

Actually, both are well supported. The main hypothesis could be the insertion of the five-activity alternative block between A43 and A28, with the A06 insertion as a second difference. Or I could combine them as "two new segments were inserted". The instructions say one main hypothesis, other differences separately. Let me make the five-activity block the main hypothesis (it has the most items), and A06's insertion as another difference under "Other differences".

Hmm, but actually, are they really separate? Let me think about whether A06's change could be part of the same underlying change. A06 is not connected to A43/A28 chain per the evidence. REL006/007 show A06 & A28 and A06 & A43 co-occurrence rose from 9% to 26.5% — but that's just because A06 participation rose; A28 and A43 are in every trace. B_before_A (A28 before A06, A43 before A06) rose — consistent with A06 being late in the trace. So A06's increase is independent of the new block (they co-occur only ~5%, less than expected if independent: 0.265 × 1.0 ≈ 26.5% expected if independent... wait, the new block is in 100% of traces, so if A06 were independent of which new activity, A06 & A19 co-occurrence should be ~22%. But it's only 4.5%!).

Hmm interesting. REL001: A06 & A19 co-occurrence after = 0.045. But A19 is in 22% of traces and A06 in 26.5%. If independent, co-occurrence ≈ 0.22 × 0.265 ≈ 5.8%. Oh wait, that's about right — 4.5% ≈ 5.8%. OK so they are roughly independent. I miscalculated: the block as a whole is in 100% of traces, but each individual activity only 22%, so A06 & A19 co-occurrence ~5.8% expected under independence. Observed 4.5%. Fine, roughly independent.

So the two changes are separate: (1) five-way alternative block between A43 and A28, present in every after-trace; (2) A06 inserted between A48 and A49 in ~24% of after-traces.

Now support level: The screening shows 50 items vs 0.68 expected — vastly more than chance. The evidence is direct (REL, LAG, DIR all show the insertion directly), consistent (many items agree), and rules out alternatives (e.g., it's not a mere frequency shift of existing paths because the five activities were absent before — zero participation — and A43→A28 direct edge essentially disappeared, going from 95% to 1%). This is "activities were added/became mandatory" territory, not a path-frequency shift. The hypothesis: a new stage of five alternative activities inserted between A43 and A28.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" level? The evidence: direct relational evidence (REL013/014/020/021 show A43 before new activity before A28; LAG002 shows the distance change; DIR007 shows A43 now routes to the five; DIR002-005 show the five route to A28). Consistent across many items. The screening count is ~73× the chance expectation. I'd say Supported hypothesis.

For the main hypothesis, limitations: we only see position-based and relation-based evidence; the five alternatives each appear in ~18-23% of traces with substantial support (35-45 traces), so that's solid. Competing explanation: could the five activities have existed before but not been observed? Before support is 0-2 traces out of 200 — participation 0-1%. If the true rate were, say, 1%, we'd expect ~2 in 200. Going from ~0-1% to ~18-23% is a big change; the "absent before" could in principle be a rare variant sampling issue, but with 200 traces and 0 observations, the rate before was very low. The screening comparison already accounts for chance. Also the empirical strength 0.995 for all items — but that's uniform, likely because all these are large changes.

The instructions: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:' without adding their activities to the main hypothesis."

So structure:

### Observed differences

Bullets:
1. Five activities A19, A20, A25, A26, A27 were absent (or nearly so) before — 0-2 of 200 traces — and in the later window each appears in about 18-23% of traces, with exactly one of them per trace (pairwise co-occurrence near 0, "neither" shares match exactly-one pattern). [OCC002-006, REL009-012, REL017-019, REL024-026]

2. These five sit between A43 and A28: before, A43 led directly to A28 in ~95% of its outgoing transitions at distance 1; after, A43 leads to one of the five (~97% combined) and each of the five leads to A28 (~95-98%); A43→A28 distance shifted from 1 step (95%) to 2 steps (96.5%). REL confirms A43 before the new activity before A28 in ~22% of traces each. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR002-005, LAG002, REL013, REL014, REL020, REL021]

3. A06: participation rose from ~9% to ~26.5% of traces; position moved from mid-trace (mean ~0.54) to near the end (median ~0.97); its outgoing transitions now go to A49 in ~89% (before ~26%); A48 now leads to A06 in ~24% of its outgoing transitions (before ~2.5%); A48→A49 distance shifted from lag 1 (95%) to lag 1 (76%)/lag 2 (24%). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR008, LAG003, REL008]

Maybe also mention A06 & A28/A43/A48 co-occurrence rise — but that's a consequence of A06's participation rise; keep it brief.

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: In the later window, a new stage of five mutually exclusive activities (A19, A20, A25, A26, A27) is executed between A43 and A28: before, A43 was followed directly by A28 (about 95 in 100 of A43's outgoing transitions, one step apart); after, A43 is followed by one of the five (about 97 in 100 combined), which then leads to A28, two steps apart. Each alternative is taken in roughly 18-23 of 100 traces. Supporting signs: direct relational and distance evidence (A43 before the new activity, the new activity before A28; A43→A28 distance moved from 1 to 2), consistent across occurrence, direction, position and relation items; the number of qualified items (50) is far above the ~0.68 expected without change.
